newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila buyers out of market after spate of orders.
newsitem.headline: Manila buyers out of market after spate of orders.

text.p: Philippine importers will probably stay out of the grains and oilseeds market next week because they have ample supplies after a recent spate of orders, traders said on Friday.
"Major Philippine flour millers have made orders up to May 15 this year," one senior Japanese trader said in describing the coverage put on by the Manila-based flour companies.
"But local buyers may be forced back into the market and buy their June requirements if prices really fall to interesting levels," the trader added.
Two Philippine flour millers had clinched deals last Wednesday to buy 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat and 15,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said.

The purchases were divided into about 45,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, 14 percent protein content, and priced at US$191 a tonne and around 15,000 tonnes of western white wheat at $165 per tonne.
There was no price available for the U.S. soybeans although U.S. beans coming into Southeast Asia fetch a quote on Thursday of $355-$360 a tonne C&F for May/June delivery on a Panamax.

Traders said the wheat orders, for April 15 to May 15 shipment, were placed through a U.S.-based commodity house and a Japanese trading firm. The soybean order was also coursed through the same U.S.-based commodity house, traders said.
The Philippines also confirmed last Monday that it had bought 100,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat at $185 per tonne FOB for May/July shipment.
The government's National Food Authority (NFA) had also purchased 25,000 tonnes of white corn from the U.S. at $201.80 a tonne through Continental Grains Co.
The Department of Trade and Industry said local flour prices remained steady at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag of hard flour and 260 pesos per 25-kg of soft flour.
The NFA said about 45,143 tonnes of rice imported from the Philippines' neighbours had already arrived out of total imports of 655,000 tonnes.
Most of the country's rice imports were bought from Thailand, Vietnam, China and Pakistan.
Some 118,658 tonnes of yellow corn imported by the NFA from China has likewise reached the Philippines.
The average retail price of yellow corn dropped to 9.89 pesos a kg from last week's 9.93 pesos while the average retail price of white corn inched up to 10.07 pesos a kg from 10.06.
